Choices the task and checklist left open:
- **Dates:** a nested `Date` is copied, since TOML settings can hold dates.
- **Other nested objects:** a class instance, `Map`, `Set`, regex or function inside the settings throws a `TypeError`, because it cannot be copied without sharing it.
- **Prototype-less objects:** objects made with `Object.create(null)` count as plain and come out as ordinary objects.
- **Cycles:** settings that contain themselves are not handled and overflow the stack.

## textwrap
The README set no requirements for wrapping, so the behaviour is my choice. I added `wrapText(text, width)` in `src/wrap.mjs`, tests in `tests/wrap.test.mjs`, and a short section in `README.md`.

- It returns one string with lines joined by `\n`, and no line is longer than `width`.
- Words on a line are joined by one space, and each line is trimmed, so leading indentation is dropped.
- Line breaks already in the text are kept, so paragraphs and blank lines survive.
- A word longer than `width` is cut into `width`-sized pieces.
- Width is counted in code points, so an emoji is not split, but wide and combining characters are not measured as terminal columns.
- A non-string `text` or non-integer `width` throws a `TypeError`; a `width` below 1 throws a `RangeError`.

## csvline
I rewrote `parseCsvLine` in `src/csv.mjs` as a single pass over the text. It now enforces the whole README contract: the old version accepted stray quotes, unclosed quotes and bare line breaks, and took quadratic time on long input.

`tests/csv.test.mjs` keeps the four original tests and adds 15:
- one group per contract line;
- a seeded round-trip test (write fields out, parse them back);
- a seeded test over 20,000 random strings that the outcome is always fields or a `CsvError`;
- a timing test over 18 shapes of 100 KB record, which all finish in about 40 ms together.

## semver-mini
I implemented `compare` in `src/semver.mjs`; the test file is untouched. Numbers are compared as digit strings, so versions beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` still order correctly. A non-string argument throws a `TypeError` before any validity check. I did not read or run the held-out cases; beyond the given tests I only spot-checked a handful of my own edge cases.
